To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the responses to chemotherapy of rat bronchial cancer growing in the lung are less than those of the same tumours growing sub-cutaneously, and that the responses vary widely between different tumour lines, even when the histology of the tumour is identical.
the responses of rat bronchial cancer lines to chemotherapy vary considerably between lines, and that responses are generally lower when tumours are implanted in the lung rather than subcutaneously.
the growth delay of tumours growing in the lung was generally less than that of the same tumours growing sub-cutaneously, and that TCNU and ifofamide were the most active drugs tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an animal model for the study of chemotherapy of non-small-cell lung cancer.
the study of the response of rat bronchial tumours to cytostatic drugs and their use as a model of human lung cancer.
the development of new drugs and drug combinations for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of chemotherapy of bronchial cancer in the rat lung are less than those obtained in the flank and the results of chemotherapy in the flank are less than those reported for the mouse.
there are substantial differences between rat bronchial carcinomas of different grades of differentiation in their response to chemotherapy.

the results of this study indicate that the response to chemotherapy of bronchial tumours growing sub-cutaneously or in the lungs depends on the tumour line used, the drug and its dose, the route of administration and whether the tumour is implanted sub-cutaneously or into the lungs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general, the more differentiated the tumour the more responsive it was to chemotherapy, and that the response of tumours growing in the lung was generally less than that of the same tumours growing in flank sites.
the growth of rat bronchial carcinomas is sensitive to chemotherapy and that the response to chemotherapy depends upon the tumour line used.
there was no single drug or combination of drugs which gave consistently high growth delays in all the tumours.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the most appropriate chemotherapeutic agent for treatment of lung cancer should be based on the tumour line used for testing.
the response to chemotherapy of bronchial tumours growing in the lung is less than that of the flank implants.
it is essential to use a range of different tumour lines in preclinical studies to assess the potential efficacy of a chemotherapeutic agent.
